request: Choose local sounds from this brief with onset, duration and volume. Use soundpilot export_copy to apply into a duplicate. Captions do not establish visual-only events; request a local storyboard only if necessary. Do not use computer control. No OpenAI API calls. Follow user_style before generic sound-name associations. Annotate each effect with function and the exact spoken/visual cue. Agreement uses MMMMMM; funny lines use FAH. Do not infer artistic accuracy from schema checks. Set style_profile_version to the active version. Do not fill quiet gaps or meet a palette quota. Rare-context sounds require context_evidence with kind, strength=high, cue and why_this_sound; otherwise omit them. For each MMMMMM cue, annotate evaluation_polarity as positive or explicit_affirmation after resolving the referenced object/context. Agreement that an option is uncomfortable/bad is negative appraisal, not MMMMMM. Not-bad/dont-mind can still be positive.

timing_policy: Identify the particular word/reaction beat, not the whole caption label.
Observed approval alignment: nice at 11.61s -> MMMMMM at 11.67s; castle at 36.60s -> 36.63s; fire at 35.30s -> 35.43s. These illustrate word alignment, not a universal delay.
A caption can contain confusion followed by approval; select different cues at their own times.
Use reaction dialogue to choose approval/comedy cues. Use the second video to establish reveal/danger/irony context.
Do not automatically sound every caption, oh, bro or scene cut.
If event function is ambiguous, flag it for review rather than inventing a generic sound.

sound_functions.rule: Continued unsettling reaction following suspense. Only one example, exact interpretation remains tentative. Require real supported unsettling context; a generic this-is-bad line in the word game was rejected.

Genuine agreement, liking, or accepting an option. Neutral okay/excited wow differ. A funny confession can take FAHH instead, even if it ends with acceptance; the user corrected failed-everything to FAHH. Positive wording alone is insufficient: the user gave I-would-too a dry awkward cue in the shopping-cart scene. Do not confuse negative appraisal with approval: agreeing that a glass cart does not look comfortable uses error. Resolve context/polarity first.

Dubious, unsettling, suspicious or ironic context. Not automatic cheating = Among Us. Positive-looking words can be sarcastic in context. Ordinary I-say-it-every-day is insufficient; that added layer was removed. The banana/date conditional-positive cue was replaced by Undertaker in test 3; do not infer innuendo/suspicion from fruit/date wording alone.
Stronger impressed visual admiration, such as mansion/rare card/Ferrari/Lamborghini. A mild oh/recognition can instead use ooooo. The car revision replaced Ferrari ooooo with anime-wow.

Deadpan, awkward pause, flat observation or skeptical setup. Do not replace a clear positive acceptance with this. Can also punctuate a dry conversational assent/echo (I would too), not only negative/hesitant wording.

A short what/no/never-mind realization, inconsistency or rejection beat. Separate the initial confusion from later approval in the same caption. Includes agreement with a negative assessment of an option, such as it does not look comfortable at all.
Actual disgust, eww, dirty/gross substance, or revulsion. Distinguish it from ordinary disagreement.
Funny confession, comic delivery, roast or absurd punchline. Latest confirmed example: I failed everything -> FAHH at 20.60s. Do not use it on every negative word or force a quota.
Longer FAH variant for a stronger/longer comic disgust line; only one observed use.
A selective exceptional-good reveal: chocolate caramel egg after bad snacks, and the Koenigsegg car reveal. Can be a quiet longer bed with a short reveal hit and a later approval cue.
One short cartoon beat before a clam-shell realization. No evidence to use it for every bro.

Short dramatic setup/opening or a scene reset. One use is mid-video, so this is not a mandatory intro sound. No automatic opening/list cue; the user removed the added setup sting in test 2. Also a short dramatic punctuation/transition near a hype yo after Lamborghini; not only opening setup.

Mild reaction lift, anticipation or recognition. Not every excited iconic reveal: Ferrari became anime-wow, Supra became a boom, and a mild December oh used ooooo. Distinguish a real reaction lift from conversationally reading an option name: gaming-cart recognition was left quiet, isolated ball-pit oh retained ooooo.
One specific positive/comic reaction. Not the main approval sound.
A tense or unsettling surprise/transition into a shocking option. Often leads the spoken reaction; not every oh-wait rethink.

A bad/dangerous/fatal-feeling option or dramatic doom reaction; inferred from three examples. Do not infer doom from cooked or a banned-word habit alone; both bells were removed in test 2. Also observed on the specific lifelong absurd banana-car consequence at 70.67s. Context is broader than literal physical danger, but cooked/habit words alone remain insufficient.
Punchy emphasis on a surprising reveal, amount, key word, or emphatic decision; can be positive or negative. Do not put it on every cut.

selection_refinements: Neutral okay is not genuine approval by itself.
Positive excitement and accepting an option are distinct: ooooo vs MMMMMM in the new manual example.
Recognizing an option (breakfast) is not the same as approving it; a boom may emphasize the noun.
Do not add a sound for every positive/negative utterance. The user selected 12 moments, leaving other lines without a cue.
Caption positions can drift independently of the video/audio. Prefer validated speech-word alignment for learning.
A funny confession can use FAHH even when followed by acceptance. The failed-everything example is now confirmed FAHH by the user.
There is no fixed FAHH quota: use a funny/roast beat when supported by delivery or a learned manual example.
Do not force Undertaker/Among Us/creepy/movie to satisfy a varied palette. This user revision removed all five such forced placements.
If a cue is removed, preserve silence unless the user supplies a replacement; do not auto-fill the gap.
A mild oh/realization can use ooooo: the user added it at 17.20s.
Suspense moved from 33.73s to 35.93s: use the actual this-is-bad beat, not the first oh.
MMMMMM moved to 47.50s after exactly; awkward moved to 60.97s at the beginning of the like-every-sentence thought.
Latest explicit instruction: when the speaker says eww, place ewww.mp3 at that spoken beat, using captions/word alignment even if ASR misses the exclamation.
Excitement has levels: Ferrari/Lamborghini admiration can use anime-wow; a mild oh can use ooooo; a named-car impact can use vine boom.
Specific exceptional-car beauty can support a heavenly bed plus a short reveal hit and later spoken approval. Distinct functions justify those layers; palette variety does not.
Banana-car deadpan confusion used awkward, not a shock boom; the lifelong absurd-car consequence used Undertaker, not inferred romantic Among Us.
The user added a short movie punctuation beat near 94.37s after the Lamborghini hype. Movie is not globally banned and is not an automatic intro.
Spoken-eww determines the sound file, not an immutable caption-start time: the user moved ewww from 8.40s to 7.97s to lead the disgust beat.
Approval and funny-line mappings remain primary. Respect user volume corrections per asset; do not make all wow sounds equally loud.
Distinguish conversational recognition from an expressive isolated oh. The gaming-cart ooooo was removed, while ball-pit ooooo was retained.
Positive sentence meaning alone does not identify the sound: I-would-too used awkward as a dry echo in this scene, while active that-is-fire approval retained MMMMMM.
The glass-cart suspense was moved to 24.90s to follow the actual reveal rather than waiting until the later spoken objection.
Place funny-word attacks around the salient syllable: user moved cooked FAHH to 31.37s and the ball-pit oh lift to 33.17s.
The teddy-cart ending remained a restrained awkward cue; do not invent stronger admiration solely from a cozy-looking prop.
Resolve appraisal polarity before MMMMMM. The uncomfortable-glass-cart line was explicitly corrected from MMMMMM to error at 27.83s.

For future edits, avoid treating awkward-moment as the default reaction/question sound. Actively compare Among Us, Undertaker, sudden suspense, huh, yeahoo and Patrick Yeah with the full scene and delivery; select whichever fits best. This is not an instruction to force every sound or a palette quota.

For future zooms, hold the complete meaningful reaction/punchline and its natural settling beat. Avoid a jarring brief punch-in that starts late on a final syllable and immediately returns. Choose the visual hold separately from the SFX length, without a fixed minimum/quota or extending across unrelated options.

Exclude the added timeline music from this Day2 SFX revision assessment and preference learning; preserve the actual saved edits. Learn SFX choices, onsets, trims, envelopes and asset levels, not the added music.

selection_policy.primary_goal: Match meaningful reaction beats; silence is a valid decision.
selection_policy.rare_sound_requirement: Require a specific supported scene/intent and exact cue; a negative word, mood label, or desire for variety is insufficient.
selection_policy.timing: Anchor the intended beat. Do not choose the first oh or always place sounds after a sentence.
selection_policy.latest_explicit_palette_preference: Consider Among Us, Undertaker, sudden suspense, huh, yeahoo and Patrick Yeah from scene/delivery; avoid overusing awkward; no compulsory palette quota.

appraisal_policy.first_step: Resolve what the speaker is evaluating and whether the completed meaning accepts or rejects it.
appraisal_policy.negative_agreement: Agreeing that the glass cart is not comfortable is a negative appraisal. Use the learned rejection cue, not MMMMMM.
appraisal_policy.positive_qualified: Not bad / I do not mind that can express positive acceptance; do not use a raw not-word filter.
appraisal_policy.explicit_affirmation: Exactly can be explicit affirmation, but do not infer it from any negative statement that happens to echo the narrator.
